newsitem.title: UK: London gold still drifts, sees fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: London gold still drifts, sees fresh demand.

text.p: London gold and silver were quiet on Monday with dealers expecting no drastic moves in the near term after gains from a moderate rally eroded late last week.
Gold prices would likely remain strangled within the broader $380-$385 price range until after the expiration of over-the-counter options on Tuesday, dealers said.
"The range is going to be $381.50 to $384.50 till after the expiry," one said. Options give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell gold at a given price at a future date.
Bullion fixed at $382.80 an ounce, compared to $382.55 an ounce on Friday afternoon.
Prices had edged up overnight on Chinese and Japanese buying, peaking at around $383.20 an ounce, dealers said.
Demand for gold in India, the world's biggest consumer of the metal, has also picked up in recent days ahead of the upcoming Diwali festival of lights, analysts said.

But a statement from Portugal's economy minister that the country may sell some of its gold reserves injected a note of wariness into the market, a dealer said. Prices shed $0.50 after the statement before recovering.
An official Bank of Portugal source then said the bank had received no indication from the government to sell reserves.
"The statement has woken the market up a bit. The news isn't bearish because it's unsubstantiated but it takes out any bullish sentiment from the market. It stops incentive," a dealer said.

Silver was also little changed, indicated up one cent at $4.92/$4.94 an ounce. Like gold, it was expected to stay within a tight range ahead of the options expiry, with the psychological $5.00 level capping attempts to move higher.
"It couldn't break through the well-defended $5.00 area last week, and on the downside support is at $4.85," a dealer said.
Platinum, which sank below the price of gold on Friday for the first time in three years was indicated barely changed from Friday's London close at $383.00/$384.00 an ounce.

Analysts said Friday's sell-off of platinum was due to the market being oversupplied and disillusioned. But it was finding support at current price levels and its discount to gold was unlikely to get much wider, they added.
Palladium was down 25 cents at $116.00/$117.00, heading back to recent lows after an attempt to edge towards $120 resistance last week fizzled out.
Its technical indicators looked increasingly bearish with the 10-day moving average close to crossing the 30-day indicator on the downside, analysts said.
